blocks.text: IN THE HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT MADRAS

Whereas on the {{ presentation_date }} the above named Plaintiff instituted a suit in our said Court against you by presenting a Plaint whereby he claims the relief whereof the short particulars are endorsed herein (or annexed hereto). We command you to appear before the Court at the hour of 10.15 A.M. in the forenoon of the day two weeks after service of the summons upon you, in person or by Attorney or Counsel, to answer the Plaintiff's claim and to bring with you any documents in your possession or power relating to the merits of the Plaintiff's case or upon which you intend to rely in support of your defence, and take notice that in default of your so doing the suit will be heard and determined in your absence.

And also take notice that if you intend to defend the suit you must cause an appearance to be entered on your behalf and file in the Court a written statement stating the grounds of your defence within two weeks after service of the summons upon you, in which case the suit will be entered in the general list of causes.
And also take notice that leave to institute this suit in this Court was granted by order dated {{ leave_order_date }} and that you are at liberty to apply to this Court to stay the said proceeding.

You are also hereby informed that you may resort to one of the modes of alternative dispute resolution as provided under Section 89 of CPC, namely (a) Arbitration, (b) Conciliation, (c) Judicial Settlement including settlement through Lok Adalat, or (d) Mediation.
Witness: THE HONOURABLE {{ chief_justice_name }}, Chief Justice at Madras, the {{ seal_date }}.
N.B.: 1. The Summons shall be served within 14 days from the date hereof.
2. The Summons was taken out by {{ advocate }}, Counsel for the said Plaintiff, whose address for service is: {{ advocate_chamber }}
CONCISE STATEMENT OF THE CLAIM MADE

And further interest at {{ interest_rate }} percent per annum until payment and Rs. {{ costs_amount }} costs. If the amount claimed be paid before the time limited for the appearance of the defendant, further proceedings will be stayed.
I hereby acknowledge service of this summons.
The summons was served by {{ served_by }}, an officer of the Sheriff (or the Court of the Munsiff of {{ munsiff_court_place }}) on {{ service_date }}.
Hours of attendance at {{ registrar_office }} office of the Registrar in the High Court Buildings, Madras, from 10.15 a.m. till 4 p.m., Sundays and holidays excepted.

uncertain: The existing 'summons' doc type may be a generic court summons; this Madras High Court Original Side summons (with leave-to-sue clause, concise statement of claim, acknowledgment and Sheriff's service endorsement) was treated as a distinct type — advocate to confirm.

The leave-to-institute paragraph is printed unconditionally as in the source; it is only apt where leave to sue (e.g. under Clause 12 of the Letters Patent) was obtained and may need to be struck out otherwise.
The Witness clause's printed 'One Thousand Nine Hundred' is an outdated date stub; replaced by a single date-of-issue field.
The blank before 'office of the Registrar' is interpreted as the name of the section/office of attendance (e.g. Original Side).
summary: This is the writ of summons issued by the High Court of Judicature at Madras on its Ordinary Original Civil Jurisdiction, commanding the defendant to appear, file a written statement and produce documents, with the concise statement of the claim, acknowledgment of service and service endorsement on the reverse. It is taken out by the plaintiff's counsel and issued under the Court's seal after a civil suit is instituted on the Original Side.
